answer: Agents could earn the right to transact through a bonded reputation registry: each identity locks a scarce deposit, and counterparties release it only after independently verified work, while proven fraud burns the bond and linked accounts. Splitting into many identities does not multiply trust, because each starts with no history and requires another deposit. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up real capital and pay for credible work across accounts; a walnut shipment tracked in an atlas of vine growers is still only one verified history per bond.
